what_its_for: Ponesimod is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) in adults. This includes clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting MS, and active secondary progressive MS. It helps reduce how often MS attacks (relapses) happen and slows down the buildup of disability.
how_to_take: Take ponesimod by mouth once a day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or split it. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can cause your MS symptoms to come back or get worse.
dosing: You will start on a low dose and gradually increase it over 14 days. This is called the 'starter pack' or titration period. This slow increase helps protect your heart when you first start the medicine. After the 14-day starter period, your maintenance (regular) dose will be 20 mg once daily. Your doctor or pharmacist will give you a calendar card to guide you through the starting doses each day.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose during the first 14 days (starter period), call your doctor before taking your next dose — you may need to restart the titration schedule from the beginning, especially if you miss more than one day. If you miss a dose after you are on the regular 20 mg dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your usual time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store ponesimod at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Keep the medicine in its original packaging. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid live vaccines (such as shingles vaccine or yellow fever vaccine) while taking ponesimod and for at least 1 to 2 weeks after stopping, unless your doctor says it is okay. Avoid being around people who are sick with infections if possible, since this medicine can lower your immune system. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or have vision changes. Tell your doctor about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, as some medicines can interact with ponesimod, especially heart medicines or medicines that slow the heart rate.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: a very slow or irregular heartbeat, chest pain, or shortness of breath (especially when starting the medicine); sudden vision changes or blurred vision (a sign of a rare but serious eye problem called macular edema); signs of infection such as fever, chills, body aches, or unusual tiredness; signs of a serious brain infection called PML, such as sudden weakness on one side of the body, trouble speaking, or confusion; new or worsening shortness of breath; skin rash or yellowing of the skin or eyes (signs of liver problems); or if your MS symptoms suddenly get much worse after stopping the medicine.
when_it_works: Ponesimod starts working in your body fairly quickly, but you may not notice changes in your MS symptoms right away. Most people begin to see benefits — such as fewer relapses — over several months of treatment. It is important to keep taking it every day even if you feel well, because it is working in the background to protect your nervous system.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do not use ponesimod if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it may harm the unborn baby. Use effective birth control while taking this medicine and for at least 1 week after stopping. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children under 18 years old. Older adults: Use with caution; your doctor may monitor your heart more closely. Liver problems: If you have severe liver disease, you should not take this medicine. Your doctor will review your medical history before prescribing it. Heart conditions: If you have certain heart rhythm problems or a very slow heart rate, your doctor may need to monitor your heart closely when you start this medicine.
